title: S4 Rational Expressions: Gap Drill
subtitle: Factor-First · LCD · Sign Distribution · 12 Questions · ~45 min
purpose: Targeted drill built from Assessment 2A misses (7/16, 44%). Three gap areas: (1) factor-first simplification — Kai tried term-by-term cancellation on Q13, fundamental misconception; (2) LCD addition/subtraction — 25% on S4.b; (3) sign distribution errors on subtraction/expansion. Weighted 5-4-3 toward factoring since it's foundational.

questions.hint: Factor BOTH the numerator and denominator completely before canceling anything. Top is a difference of squares. Bottom is a trinomial.
questions.feedback_correct: Factor first, cancel second. Never cancel individual terms.
questions.feedback_wrong: Factor top: (x+2)(x-2). Factor bottom: (x+2)(x+3). Cancel the (x+2). Answer: (x-2)/(x+3).

questions.hint: Top: pull out x first, then factor what's left. Bottom: factor the trinomial. Do NOT cancel x^3 → x or x^2 → 1. That's not how fractions work.
solution_steps: Numerator: x^3 - 4x = x(x^2 - 4) = x(x-2)(x+2)    [GCF then diff of squares]
questions.feedback_correct: GCF first, then difference of squares. Cancel common FACTORS only.
questions.feedback_wrong: Top: x(x^2-4) = x(x-2)(x+2). Bottom: (x-2)(x+1). Cancel (x-2). Answer: x(x+2)/(x+1). You CANNOT cancel individual terms like x^3→x.

questions.question_html:
Simplify by factoring first:
\( \dfrac{x^2 + x}{x^2 - 1} \)
Reminder: Factor completely before canceling.
questions.hint: Top: factor out x. Bottom: difference of squares. Then cancel the common factor.
questions.feedback_correct: This is similar to Assessment Q1. Factor both, cancel (x+1).
questions.feedback_wrong: Top: x(x+1). Bottom: (x+1)(x-1). Cancel (x+1). Answer: x/(x-1). NOT x/(x-1) = -1.

questions.hint: Top: GCF of 2, then difference of squares. Bottom: factor the trinomial — what two numbers multiply to 8 and add to -6?
questions.feedback_wrong: Top: 2(x^2-4) = 2(x+2)(x-2). Bottom: (x-4)(x-2). Cancel (x-2). Answer: 2(x+2)/(x-4). Assessment Q7 had the same factoring in the denominator.

questions.question_html:
Simplify by factoring first:
\( \dfrac{x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x}{x^2 + 4x + 3} \)
Warning: If you try to cancel individual terms without factoring, you WILL get the wrong answer.
questions.hint: Top: pull out x first to get x(x^2+2x-3), then factor the quadratic. Bottom: factor the trinomial. Then cancel.
solution_steps: Numerator: x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x = x(x^2 + 2x - 3) = x(x+3)(x-1)   [GCF then factor]
questions.feedback_correct: Same pattern as Assessment Q13. GCF → factor → cancel FACTORS.
questions.feedback_wrong: Top: x(x+3)(x-1). Bottom: (x+3)(x+1). Cancel (x+3). Answer: x(x-1)/(x+1). You cannot cancel x^3→x or x^2→1 — those are TERMS, not FACTORS.

questions.question_html:
Add. Write your answer as a single fraction in simplest form:
\( \dfrac{3}{x+2} + \dfrac{5}{x-1} \)
questions.hint: LCD = (x+2)(x-1). Multiply first fraction top and bottom by (x-1). Multiply second by (x+2). Combine numerators.
questions.feedback_correct: LCD, multiply, combine, simplify. Watch signs when distributing.

questions.question_html:
Subtract. Write your answer as a single fraction in simplest form:
\( \dfrac{4x}{x+1} - \dfrac{3}{x+4} \)
questions.hint: LCD = (x+1)(x+4). After multiplying, the SUBTRACTION means you negate ALL terms from the second numerator: -(3)(x+1) = -3x - 3, not -3x + 3.
questions.feedback_correct: Key step: distribute the negative to ALL terms. -3(x+1) = -3x - 3.
questions.feedback_wrong: LCD = (x+1)(x+4). Top: 4x(x+4) - 3(x+1) = 4x^2+16x-3x-3 = 4x^2+13x-3. The minus sign hits BOTH terms.

questions.hint: LCD of 2x^2 and 4x^3 is 4x^3. Multiply the first fraction by 2x/2x.
questions.feedback_correct: Same idea as Assessment Q6c. LCD with monomials — match the highest power of each factor.

questions.hint: LCD = (x-3)(x+1). Distribute carefully: the second numerator becomes -2(x-3) = -2x + 6, NOT -2x - 6.
questions.feedback_correct: The trap: -2(x-3) = -2x + 6, not -2x - 6. Distribute the negative to BOTH terms.
questions.feedback_wrong: -2(x-3) = -2x+6. The minus flips the -3 to +6. Full numerator: x^2+x-2x+6 = x^2-x+6.

questions.hint: FOIL (2x+1)(2x+1) FIRST. Then multiply the entire result by 3. Do not distribute the 3 into the parentheses before squaring.
questions.feedback_correct: Square first, then multiply. This is what Assessment Q5 tested.

questions.question_html:
Simplify the difference quotient:
\( \dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} \) where \( f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x + 1 \)
Show all expansion steps. Watch your coefficients.
questions.hint: f(x+h) = 3(x+h)^2 - 2(x+h) + 1. Expand (x+h)^2 = x^2+2xh+h^2 first. Then multiply by 3 — the 3 hits ALL three terms. Subtract f(x). Cancel. Divide by h.
questions.feedback_wrong: 3(x+h)^2 = 3x^2+6xh+3h^2, NOT 3x^2+2xh+h^2. The 3 multiplies EVERY term. Then subtract f(x), divide by h.

questions.hint: LCD = (x+1)(x+4). Multiply each numerator by the other denominator. When subtracting, distribute the negative to EVERY term in the second numerator.
solution_steps: Second numerator: (x-2)(x+1) = x^2 + x - 2x - 2 = x^2 - x - 2
